opening.text: A slinky. A strand of spaghetti. A jar of nuts. A coffee drop. A cup of water. And a raindrop. Six ordinary things. Each one hides a reason that is too quick, too small, or too hidden to see. So we'll slow each one down, until the physics shows.

sentences.text: A slinky.
A strand of spaghetti.
A jar of nuts.
A coffee drop.
A cup of water.
And a raindrop.
Six ordinary things.
Each one hides a reason that is too quick, too small, or too hidden to see.
So we'll slow each one down, until the physics shows.

bridge1.text: The slinky's bottom waited, because the news of the drop had to travel down it, like a wave. A bending stick has the same problem. When it snaps, a wave from the break runs along it, and that wave can break it again.

sentences.text: The slinky's bottom waited, because the news of the drop had to travel down it, like a wave.
A bending stick has the same problem.
When it snaps, a wave from the break runs along it, and that wave can break it again.

bridge2.text: Spaghetti breaks into a few pieces. Now let's watch a whole jar of pieces at once. Shake it, and something strange happens to the biggest one.

sentences.text: Spaghetti breaks into a few pieces.
Now let's watch a whole jar of pieces at once.
Shake it, and something strange happens to the biggest one.

bridge3.text: In the jar, the big nut rises because small grains slip into the gaps under it. Small things moving together can do surprising things. So can the tiny specks inside a drop of drying coffee.

sentences.text: In the jar, the big nut rises because small grains slip into the gaps under it.
Small things moving together can do surprising things.
So can the tiny specks inside a drop of drying coffee.

bridge4.text: The coffee drop hid a flow that carries its specks to the edge. Now let's listen for a different hidden shape: the empty air inside a cup.

sentences.text: The coffee drop hid a flow that carries its specks to the edge.
Now let's listen for a different hidden shape: the empty air inside a cup.

bridge5.text: A cup's note climbs as its empty space shrinks. For the last one, water is falling through the air instead, from a cloud.

sentences.text: A cup's note climbs as its empty space shrinks.

finale.text: A slinky that waits. A stick that breaks again. A nut that rises. A ring from a drop. A cup that sings. A raindrop with a speed limit. None of them needed new physics, only a slower look. And all of them were happening around you the whole time. Next time you see something ordinary, slow it down in your head.
